placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_west_randolph_des_plaines, the block's Randolph Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its west wall is fixed by the west end of the run's own frontage, 1.5 m clear of the side lot line at that end. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at Randolph Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.
placement.symbolic_location: Anonymous reconstructed roof in the West Division block bounded by Randolph, Jefferson, Washington and Des Plaines; standing ON the Randolph Street frontage itself, one unit of the party-line row along it

residents.basis: KEPT HERE BY THE DEAL, NOT RECORDED HERE (L358). This keeper's trade is one the premises ruling gives a house of its own, and no source says where it stood; this is the nearest empty roof of that trade in their division. The roof is the invention and the keeper is not.

persons.note: RECONSTRUCTED, NOT FOUND. Nobody is named by any source here. This person exists because the town model says the town of 1 July 1835 employed more people than its rosters print, and the whole of what is claimed is that: an adult of this sex and band, in the west division, at carpenter. The trade is dealt from the 1839 directory's shares and the person is reproducible from the seeds printed above. A real name retires them. No figure is drawn (L1).

fabric_basis.words: patched boards under a patched roof — a carpenter's shop, from the 1832–33 town (rule F-W: a tradesman's shop by its type)

frontage.why: T-0024 sends a workshop to its block's better face, and this block's better face is Randolph Street, the ordinary road west out of the town, while every West Division lot fronts the north-south street on the outer side of its column. So the carpenter's or joiner's shop does not stand on a lot frame at all: it stands in a one-lot frontage run on the Randolph face of plat lot 2, against the Des Plaines corner and on the street line, at the 1.5 m margin the plat module allows, because the placement policy's mechanics_streets clause stands a workshop at its street, where a wagon bringing timber or a customer coming out along Randolph meets it first. The run is one lot long and holds one roof; nothing is built shoulder to shoulder here, and the rest of the face stays as open as the recipe's outer edge requires.
